title: Molecular Cues from Extracellular Matrix Proteins Drive the Differentiation of Dental Pulp Stem Cells into Endothelial Cells in the Presence of Dentin Matrix Protein 1
html: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) have the potential to differentiate into endothelial cells (ECs) because they express the key cell surface markers like VEGFR1 and VE-cadherin and can be stimulated by various growth factors. We have previously demonstrated that DPSCs, when stimulated by DMP1 combined with cues from human umbilical vein endothelial cells matrix, promoted their differentiation into ECs. In this study, we explored the response of DPSCs to specific extracellular matrix components such as laminin and Matrigel combined with DMP1 stimulation.
